scenario.prompt_to_agent:
The user on pc1 (195.11.14.2) reports total network loss: they
cannot reach pc2 (200.1.1.2), and they cannot even ping their own
gateway 195.11.14.1. pc1's own NIC still shows link up. The
partner AS is healthy internally: pc2 reaches its gateway
200.1.1.1 fine. Find what broke.

injection.action: administratively down the LAN interface (eth1) toward pc1 on router1

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth1 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router1 eth1 (195.11.14.1/24, the LAN
  interface toward pc1)
Mechanism: router1's eth1 is DOWN, so pc1's only gateway address
  195.11.14.1 is gone from the segment -- pc1 cannot even ARP its
  gateway and loses all off-host connectivity. On router1 the
  connected route 195.11.14.0/24 disappears from the RIB, so the
  `network 195.11.14.0/24` statement has no matching route and
  the prefix is withdrawn from BGP -- AS 2 also loses its path to
  pc1. pc1's own NIC still shows link up (its side of the virtual
  segment is unaffected), which is why a host-side check looks
  clean. The inter-AS link and the eBGP session machinery are not
  the fault; the failure sits on the router1<->pc1 LAN leg.
Localization: router1
Root cause: router1 eth1 (LAN link to pc1) is down
Fix: `ip link set eth1 up` on router1
scenario.fix_spec:
`ip link set eth1 up` on router1. The gateway 195.11.14.1 comes back on the
segment, the connected route returns and BGP re-advertises 195.11.14.0/24
automatically; pc1 reaches pc2 normally. pc1 needs no change.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is a kernel-level administrative shutdown of router1's LAN-facing
interface eth1 (195.11.14.1/24). The interface appears in `ip addr` with
only the BROADCAST and MULTICAST flags set — it is missing both the UP and
LOWER_UP flags — meaning the OS-level link was brought down (e.g. via
`ip link set eth1 down`) and has not been restored. The IP address
195.11.14.1/24 is correctly configured on that interface, but no traffic
can pass because the interface is in the DOWN state.

This explains every aspect of the symptom exactly: pc1's NIC (eth0,
195.11.14.2/24) is fully operational and connected — packets do arrive at
router1's eth1 wire side (3 RX dropped counters confirm this) — but the
kernel discards them immediately because the interface is administratively
down. ARP requests from pc1 for the gateway 195.11.14.1 are therefore never
answered, so pc1 cannot resolve or reach its gateway, let alone any remote
destination. The BGP peering link (router1:eth0 ↔ router2:eth0) and
router2's LAN side are both healthy, confirming the fault is isolated
entirely to router1's eth1.

Root cause: router1's eth1 interface was administratively shut down at the
OS level, severing connectivity between pc1 and its gateway.

Corrective fix: On router1, run `ip link set eth1 up` to restore the
interface. To make it persistent across restarts, ensure the startup script
(e.g. router1.startup) includes the equivalent `ip link set eth1 up` or
that the interface is declared UP in the network configuration.
